title: Radical of an ideal at a minimal prime
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I an ideal and q a prime minimal over I, meaning a minimal element among prime ideals containing I. Let R_q be its localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the radical of IR_q equals qR_q. The radical consists of elements whose positive powers belong to the ideal. This applies without a Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07FJ, Ad(item-power); standard prime correspondence for localization

proof.text: Apply IsLocalization.AtPrime.radical_map_of_mem_minimalPrimes with A=R_q. Its conclusion is exactly sqrt(IR_q)=qR_q, for the localization in the statement; no Noetherian assumption is needed.
